designSummary: Two-arm parallel trial; comparison of proportions with glucose out of range on the day of surgery.
sampleSize: To detect a reduction from 34 to 20 percent with 80 percent power at a two-sided 5 percent level, about 154 patients per arm are needed ((1.96 + 0.84) squared times (0.34 x 0.66 + 0.20 x 0.80) divided by 0.14 squared), 308 in total, or about 342 allowing for 10 percent loss. At about 150 eligible patients a year and the 48 percent recruitment seen in a comparable pilot, the hospital would randomise about 72 a year, so recruitment would take nearly five years. A definitive single-site trial is not feasible; a feasibility study or a multicentre trial would be needed.
primaryAnalysis: Risk difference with 95 percent confidence interval, adjusted for specialty.
missingData: Multiple imputation if outcome completeness falls below 90 percent; completeness itself reported.
summary: About 342 patients needed; nearly five years at this hospital; a definitive single-site trial is not feasible.
